sources.name: Avalanche Metrics API
sources.authority: Ava Labs' official derived metrics behind the Avalanche explorer. Authoritative for the aggregates it defines; definitions are endpoint-specific and units are not documented, so each series is reconciled against raw-data datasets where one exists.
sources.authentication: none; the public endpoint answers keyless requests with a page limit of 2160 points, so each series is captured as fixed two-year windows
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; Ava Labs terms apply to redistribution.
notes: OpenAPI /v2/networks/{network}/metrics/{metric}: Gets staking metrics for a given subnet. NetworkMetric enum: delegatorCount, delegatorWeight, validatorCount, validatorWeight.

OpenAPI /v2/chains/{chainId}/metrics/{metric}: EVM chain metrics are available for all Avalanche L1s on Mainnet and Fuji. All metrics are updated several times every hour. Each metric data point has a value and timestamp (Unix timestamp in seconds). All metric values include data within the duration of the associated timestamp plus the requested timeInterval. All timestamps are fixed to the hour.
OpenAPI MetricsValue.value: Aggregated value for the current metrics. MetricsValue.timestamp: Unix Epoch timestamp for which metrics are aggregated; for a day interval this is the start of the day.

Chain 43114 is the C-Chain. The API serves no P-Chain chain metrics (HTTP 404 for the Primary Network subnet ID), so P-Chain fees and burn come from the Snowflake P_TRANSACTIONS columns FEE and BURNED_AVAX instead.
Both series begin 2021-01-01; earlier dates are absent from the API although the Primary Network has staking history from 2020-09-10.

Reconciliation on 2026-09-19 against the end-of-day active set rebuilt from the Snowflake validator and delegator datasets: validator counts differ by a median 1.1 percent in 2021 to 2023, 2.1 percent in 2024, 2.8 percent in 2025, and 3.4 percent in 2026; delegator counts by 1.5 to 2.4 percent in 2021 to 2022 and 5.5 to 8 percent from 2023. Sampled days in 2022 and 2024 match exactly at end of day, so the residual reflects the API's undocumented aggregation instant plus an undercount from 2025 that also skips nine days between 2025-10-12 and 2025-12-01.

sources.name: Avalanche Data API
sources.authority: Ava Labs' official indexed data behind the Avalanche explorer. Its supply endpoint reports current totals, while its C-Chain Primary Network transaction endpoint reports atomic imports and exports with AVAX input and output amounts.
sources.authentication: optional; the x-glacier-api-key header, read from the AVALANCHE_DATA_API_KEY environment variable and sent only to glacier-api.avax.network, which accepts it (the data-api.avax.network alias rejects it). Keyless requests work at a lower limit. The key is never stored in the repository, a capture, or a receipt.
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; Ava Labs terms apply to redistribution.
notes: OpenAPI GET /v1/avax/supply: Get AVAX supply information that includes total supply, circulating supply, total p burned, total c burned, total x burned, total staked, total locked, total rewards, and last updated. The operation takes no parameters.

Blocker recorded 2026-09-19: the Data API exposes no historical supply, circulating supply, staked supply, or cumulative burn series; the supply endpoint returns one current state with lastUpdated. A history can only be assembled by repeated captures or from the Snowflake block supply counter.
Observed 2026-09-19: totalSupply equals genesisUnlock plus totalRewards minus the three burn totals to within one AVAX, so the API's totals are internally consistent.

C-Chain atomic transaction listing pages backward from latest; startTimestamp and endTimestamp require an address filter, so a complete all-address dated capture walks pages until it crosses the requested start.

Validators endpoint, measured 2026-09-22: 100 rows per page is the maximum, about four seconds a page, no rate-limit headers, and Cloudflare rejects Python's default user agent. Without a subnetId filter the endpoint also returns subnet validators, which have no delegation fee. Active Primary Network validations carry uptimePerformance as observed by Ava Labs' node; completed validations carry rewards and reward addresses but no uptime, so historical uptime percentages are not recoverable from this API.

C-Chain block record, measured 2026-09-23: GET /v1/chains/43114/blocks/{height} returns the block's feesSpent, an integer number of wei equal to the sum of gas used times effective gas price over its receipts; the block listing takes no height range, so gap blocks are read one request each

Rate limit, measured 2026-09-23: keyless, the API answered HTTP 429 after about 130 requests at three a second and again after about 1,000 requests at one a second, and kept refusing for more than ten minutes; a key would raise the limit and is never stored in the repository
With a key, measured 2026-09-23: the response carries ratelimit-policy 8000;w=60, cost units per minute, and a block request costs about ten, so about 750 block requests a minute

observed_semantics: C-Chain EVM burn is the integer-wei sum of receipt gas used times effective gas price
C_BLOCKS.BLOCKTRANSACTIONLEN provides an independent expected receipt count per block and per day
The share loaded 2025-08-28 and 2025-09-07 twice: every block and receipt of those days repeats, so blocks and receipts are read once by height and transaction hash

The share lacks every receipt of 2023-10-06 and about a third of the receipts of 2023-12-13 and 2023-12-14 while holding the blocks, and lacks about fifteen thousand blocks on some forty days of 2025; the burn is summed over complete blocks only and the gaps are counted

observed_semantics: BURNED_AVAX is the transaction's AVAX destruction in nAVAX; a hash that repeats in the share is read once, taking a recorded burn over a null one
Three P-Chain ImportTx of 2022-01-15 and 2022-01-16 record a negative BURNED_AVAX; a negative record is read as no record, and the UTXO method gives each the 0.001 AVAX pre-Etna import fee

AdvanceTimeTx and RewardValidatorTx carry no burn; genesis transactions (2020-09-10, block height -1) carry none either, confirmed on all 77 P and 1 X genesis hashes against the Data API on 2026-09-21
A null burn outside those cases is inputs minus non-reward outputs over the AVAX UTXOs the share holds for the hash; the method reproduced BURNED_AVAX on 30 P and 60 X control transactions
24 P-Chain ImportTx of 2025-03-11 and 2025-03-14 consume UTXOs the share does not hold and stay unresolved; the row lists their hashes for the Data API transaction capture

For IncreaseL1ValidatorBalanceTx, RegisterL1ValidatorTx, and ConvertSubnetToL1Tx, BURNED_AVAX includes the L1 validator balance deposited (L1_VALIDATOR_PAYG_BALANCE per validator row); the deposit is subtracted from the burn and reported apart, matching the Data API's amountBurned and amountL1ValidatorBalanceBurned on ten sampled transactions

L1 validator fees accrue continuously from those balances: L1_VALIDATOR_ACCRUED_FEES is a per-validator cumulative counter and L1_VALIDATOR_ACTIVE_COUNT the validators paying it, so the fee burned between two P transactions is the previous count times the counter's increase; summed to 2026-09-19 11:00 UTC this gives 17,951.43 AVAX against the Data API's 17,951.41

The Data API's totalPBurned equals these transaction burns plus the L1 validator fees; its totalXBurned equals the recorded X burns and omits the 612 null-burn X transactions of 2025-09-13 to 2025-09-15 that the UTXO method settles at 0.679 AVAX

sources.name: Avalanche Builder Hub validator explorer
sources.authority: Ava Labs' Builder Hub, which proxies a validator-metrics service fed by the nodes Ava Labs runs. Its uptime is the hourly median across those observers: one observer set, beside the public P-Chain RPC node and the Data API, and not the protocol's own stake-weighted vote at period end.
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; no terms published for these routes. Redistribution terms unassessed.
notes: Measured 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24: the list route returns a JSON array of about 611 current Primary Network validators; the detail route returns, per node, hourly uptime buckets for a rolling window of 332 hours, daily bench totals, hourly block proposals and misses, and a 14-day summary of the underlying observations (116,017 for one node). A validator that has ended still answers.

Changed between the captures of 2026-09-27 00:45 UTC and 2026-09-29 19:17 UTC: the window is about 175 hours, each detail carries observed_at, the hours both captures hold were restated (74% of settled node-hours differ, by 0.016 percentage points on average and 11.4 at most, where consecutive captures had agreed exactly), and 10 of 11 validators that had ended answer HTTP 500.
The route caches each answer for five minutes and, when its upstream fails, answers from cache with the response header X-Data-Source: error-fallback-cache, which the capture records per node.
The routes proxy a service at a bare address (52.203.183.9.sslip.io); the capture calls the published Builder Hub routes, not the address.
The slots series (slot, count) is kept in the raw lines and not built into a table; its meaning is undocumented.

sources.name: Derived datasets
sources.authority: No external authority. A derived dataset is a deterministic transformation of built runs of other datasets in this catalog, and inherits their authority and limits. Its receipt records the exact input runs and their hashes.
sources.reuse_status: Follows the reuse status of its inputs.
notes: Built with `avalanche data derive`, which selects the newest built run of each input unless a run is pinned, and writes a capture receipt naming the input runs beside the Parquet build.
The staking-period log adds the network upgrade regime at acceptance and the reward the protocol kernel computes for each row, so the recorded potential reward can be checked row by row.

The node table folds the staking-period log, the reward addresses on validator transactions, and the delegator addresses into one row per validator node. Its clocks are clipped at the validator capture time, so a run is reproducible from its inputs alone.

The monetary daily ledger replays supply from genesis: rewards paid out minus burns on every chain, in wei, with a coverage state per component and per day, and takes every current run of the multi-run inputs so repairs captured later fill earlier gaps without a rebuild of the sources.

The hourly validator uptime table merges every Builder Hub capture into one row per node per hour, keeping the newest capture's value, the number of captures that held the hour, and whether any two disagreed. Daily captures overlap by about six days since the source shortened its window to about 175 hours, so the table grows without gaps while captures continue. Hours the source restated keep the newest value and are marked revised.

sources.authority: Each issuer's own published figures for its product: Bitwise for BAVA, VanEck for VAVX, 21Shares for its Avalanche product and two baskets that hold AVAX, and Grayscale's filings with the SEC for GAVA. The issuer is the authority for its own NAV, shares outstanding, and AVAX held. None of these is an on-chain observation.
sources.authentication: none; VanEck's blocks answer a browser User-Agent and the capture keeps one cookie jar for them, and SEC EDGAR requires a User-Agent that names a contact
sources.reuse_status: Public issuer disclosures and SEC filings. Issuer website terms govern redistribution of the web figures; SEC filings are public records.
notes: Measured 2026-09-28. bavaetf.com embeds its fund record as Next.js data in the page: net assets, shares outstanding, NAV, the AVAX units held (holdings.basket), the share staked, reward rates, 32 custody wallets with balances, and a daily NAV series since 2026-04-14. Shares outstanding and AVAX units are current only.

Measured 2026-09-28. VanEck's VAVX blocks give net assets, shares outstanding, AVAX in trust, AVAX per 1,000 shares, the share staked, staking yields, and the NAV, all as of the prior business day and current only.

Measured 2026-09-28. 21Shares' API answers gzipped JSON. product_details gives units outstanding, total NAV, and per constituent the weight, price, and AVAX entitlement per unit. product_valuation_history gives one row per valuation date since launch (2021-11-18 for AVAX) with NAV per unit, units outstanding, total NAV, the index level, and each underlying's price. MOON (Sygnum Platform Winners) and KEYS (Bitwise Select 10) are baskets in which AVAX is one constituent.

Grayscale's GAVA page refuses automated requests. Its 10-Q filings, through SEC companyfacts, give quarter-end AVAX held (InvestmentOwnedBalanceContracts), shares outstanding, NAV per share, and net assets. Where a later filing restates a period, the latest filing's value is kept. AVAX per share stays near 2.4 on every quarter end from 2024-12-31, so the filed share counts before the 1-for-5 reverse split of 2026-03-05 read as restated for it.

BAVA's wallets can be mapped to Primary Network validators through the Data API. On 2026-09-28 they staked 1,679,864 AVAX on 20 validators, 63.05% of the fund's 2,664,323 AVAX. The capture keeps the wallet list in the raw page and does not map it.

datasets.name: Primary Network staking periods
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per staking period on the Avalanche Primary Network, validators and delegators together, joined to its reward outcome and its supply reading, with the network upgrade regime at acceptance and the reward the protocol kernel computes for the row. From Helicon one auto-renewed transaction holds many cycles: its row keeps the transaction's first period, and cycles and last_cycle_end_time give the rest.

fields.name: transaction_hash
fields.derivation: the staking transaction, from validator or delegator stakes

fields.name: role
fields.derivation: which input table the row came from

fields.name: tx_type
fields.unit: one of the four staking types
fields.derivation: copied from the stake row

fields.name: node_id
fields.derivation: copied from the stake row

fields.name: validator_transaction_hash
fields.unit: P-Chain transaction ID, null for validators
fields.derivation: the delegated validator's staking transaction

fields.name: accepted_at
fields.derivation: block time the staking transaction was accepted

fields.name: block_height
fields.derivation: copied from the stake row

fields.name: start_time
fields.derivation: staking period start

fields.name: end_time
fields.derivation: staking period end

fields.name: duration_days
fields.derivation: end_time minus start_time

fields.name: stake_navax
fields.derivation: staked weight

fields.name: stake_avax
fields.derivation: stake_navax / 1e9

fields.name: potential_reward_navax
fields.derivation: reward the protocol committed to at acceptance, from the stake row

fields.name: potential_reward_avax
fields.derivation: potential_reward_navax / 1e9

fields.name: rewarded
fields.derivation: whether the period ended with a reward, from the reward row where one exists and otherwise the stake row, which a share row cannot know after the share stopped

fields.name: delegation_fee_rate
fields.derivation: validator delegation fee

fields.name: regime
fields.derivation: latest mainnet upgrade activated at accepted_at, from the protocol kernel's schedule

fields.name: start_kind
fields.derivation: pending when start_time is after accepted_at

fields.name: rewarded_at
fields.unit: UTC, null while the period is open
fields.derivation: reward transaction time from staking rewards

fields.name: realized_reward_navax
fields.derivation: minted reward from staking rewards, zero on uptime failure

fields.name: realized_reward_avax
fields.derivation: realized_reward_navax / 1e9

fields.name: fee_transfer_navax
fields.derivation: realized_reward_navax minus potential_reward_navax. Sign and meaning depend on the row: a rewarded delegation to a validator added at or after Cortina reads minus (potential reward times the validator's fee rate), the fee withheld and paid to the validator at its own period end; a rewarded delegation to a validator added before Cortina reads zero, because its reward UTXOs included the validator's share; a rewarded validator period reads plus the delegatee rewards it accrued since Cortina; any period that realised zero reads minus its potential reward. Fee income and fee paid are therefore derived from rate times potential, never read from this field (node table plan NC2, glossary G15). The derived check reconciles the post-Cortina delegations.

fields.name: supply_before_navax
fields.unit: nAVAX, null when no supply row
fields.derivation: previous block supply plus earlier in-block deltas, from staking supply

fields.name: kernel_reward_navax
fields.unit: nAVAX, null when no supply row
fields.derivation: primary_network_reward(start_time, duration, stake_navax, supply_before_navax) from the protocol kernel

fields.name: kernel_gap_navax
fields.unit: nAVAX, null when no kernel value
fields.derivation: kernel_reward_navax minus potential_reward_navax

fields.name: reproduced
fields.unit: flag, null when no kernel value
fields.derivation: kernel_reward_navax equals potential_reward_navax

fields.name: cycles
fields.derivation: 1 for an ordinary period; for an ACP-236 auto-renewed validator, the cycles its transaction has started, from derived.p-chain-staking-cycles when that table is built

fields.name: last_cycle_end_time
fields.derivation: the end of the latest cycle of an auto-renewed validator; null for an ordinary period, whose end is end_time

datasets.name: Primary Network validator nodes
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per node that has validated the Primary Network, with every attribute the studies reason about computed once: the three clocks (span, tenure, current streak) and their stake weights, stake and fee history, delegation, rewards and failures, upgrade regimes, and the reward address as an operator proxy. Clocks are clipped at the validator capture time and active nodes are right-censored. Each field names the glossary term it realises. When the day's validator snapshots exist, active nodes also carry uptime from two observers, delegation fill, node version, and country.

fields.name: node_id
fields.derivation: one row per node that has validated the Primary Network; a node is a machine identity, not an operator (glossary G1)

fields.name: as_of
fields.derivation: the validator capture time the clocks are clipped at; every duration in the row is as of this instant

fields.name: first_start
fields.derivation: start of the node's first staking period

fields.name: last_end
fields.derivation: end of the node's last staking period, which may lie after as_of

fields.name: active
fields.unit: true when last_end is after as_of
fields.derivation: the right-censoring flag: for an active node span, tenure, and current streak are lower bounds

fields.name: periods
fields.derivation: validator staking periods started before as_of (glossary G5)

fields.name: closed_periods
fields.derivation: periods with a reward transaction

fields.name: failed_periods
fields.derivation: closed periods that realised zero reward, the uptime requirement not met (glossary G13)

fields.name: streaks
fields.derivation: unbroken runs of periods; a gap of more than streak_gap_days between one period's end and the next start ends a streak (glossary G8, coined)

fields.name: gap_count
fields.derivation: streaks minus one

fields.name: gap_days
fields.derivation: total days between streaks, from a streak's clipped end to the next streak's start

fields.name: span_days
fields.derivation: first_start to last_end, or to as_of if active, gaps included (glossary G18 span, coined)

fields.name: tenure_days
fields.derivation: sum of the node's staking periods with gaps excluded and overlaps merged, clipped at as_of (glossary G17 tenure, the client's word; Stata's time at risk)

fields.name: current_streak_days
fields.derivation: length of the latest streak, clipped at as_of (glossary G8)

fields.name: stake_days_avax
fields.derivation: sum over periods of stake times clipped days; the quantity a stake-and-time reward would pay on (glossary G20, coined)

fields.name: stake_weighted_period_days
fields.derivation: stake-weighted mean length of the node's periods; a sizing statistic, not a total (glossary G21, coined)

fields.name: min_stake_avax
fields.derivation: smallest own stake across periods (glossary G22)

fields.name: max_stake_avax
fields.derivation: largest own stake across periods

fields.name: latest_stake_avax
fields.derivation: own stake of the latest period

fields.name: latest_fee_rate
fields.derivation: delegation fee rate of the latest period (glossary G12)

fields.name: fee_settings
fields.derivation: how many distinct fee rates the node has used; fee is a per-period choice, not a fixed trait

fields.name: delegations
fields.derivation: delegations to the node's periods (glossary G23)

fields.name: delegated_avax
fields.derivation: sum of delegated stake across the node's periods

fields.name: delegator_addresses
fields.derivation: sum over periods of distinct funding delegator addresses (glossary G25); a period's addresses may repeat across periods

fields.name: max_period_delegation_ratio
fields.derivation: largest over periods of delegated stake divided by delegation capacity, capacity being delegation_capacity_multiple times own stake; an upper bound on fill because delegations within a period need not overlap (glossary G24)

fields.name: rewards_avax
fields.derivation: sum of the node's own realised validation rewards (glossary G14)

fields.name: delegatee_fees_avax
fields.derivation: fee income: sum over rewarded delegations of potential reward times the period's fee rate, the convention settled for fee_transfer_navax (glossary G15)

fields.name: first_regime
fields.derivation: network upgrade regime of the first period (glossary G10, G11)

fields.name: last_regime
fields.derivation: regime of the latest period

fields.name: reward_address
fields.derivation: reward address of the latest period

fields.name: reward_addresses_used
fields.derivation: distinct reward addresses across periods

fields.name: operator_group
fields.derivation: the latest reward address, used as an operator proxy: a shared address can link nodes, but it does not prove one decision maker, and different addresses do not prove different operators (node table plan NK1, interface rule I2)

fields.name: uptime_rpc_pct
fields.derivation: the public P-Chain RPC node's observed uptime for an active node, from the newest p-chain-rpc.current-validators run when one exists; null for finished nodes and before 2026-09-22 (glossary G13)

fields.name: uptime_api_pct
fields.derivation: Ava Labs' indexer's observed uptime for an active node, from the newest data-api.validators-active run when one exists; a second observer, kept beside the first because the protocol's own view is a majority vote neither observer is

fields.name: uptime_observed_at
fields.derivation: the later of the two observer captures joined

fields.name: delegation_fill_api
fields.derivation: delegated stake over four times own stake on the active validation, from the API observer (glossary G24)

fields.name: node_version
fields.derivation: from the API observer; null when unknown

fields.name: country
fields.derivation: from the API observer's geolocation; null when unknown

datasets.name: Validator-week panel
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per Primary Network validator node per UTC week, Monday 00:00 to the next Monday, from 2020-09-21 to the last full week before Helicon (2026-09-14), for every week the node is validating at the Monday cutoff or first starts a period during it. Every feature is computed from staking transactions accepted before the cutoff, so a row does not change when later events are appended; the check rebuilds the weeks before 2025-01-06 from truncated inputs and compares them. Outcomes are the delegations accepted during the week, counted with and without the one address that made 93% of delegation events. Built for the S2 input contract of the validator study; it asserts nothing about the article's unpublished market size or sample rule.

fields.name: node_id
fields.derivation: the validator node; the unit is a node, not an operator (interface rule I2)

fields.name: week_start_utc
fields.derivation: Monday 00:00 of the week; the feature cutoff

fields.name: active_at_week_start
fields.derivation: a validator period of the node, accepted before the cutoff, spans the cutoff; false for a node whose period starts during the week

fields.name: offered_at_week_start
fields.derivation: active at the cutoff, at least 14 days left in the period, and at least 25 AVAX of delegation capacity left throughout the next 14 days; a 100% fee does not remove the offer (decision SD4)

fields.name: validator_transaction_hash
fields.derivation: the validator period active at the cutoff

fields.name: period_start
fields.derivation: start of that period

fields.name: period_end
fields.derivation: committed end of that period

fields.name: days_remaining
fields.derivation: period_end minus the cutoff

fields.name: self_stake_avax
fields.derivation: the node's own stake in the active period (glossary G22)

fields.name: delegation_fee_rate
fields.derivation: the active period's delegation fee (G12)

fields.name: first_start_known
fields.derivation: earliest start among the node's validator periods known at the week's cutoff, Monday 00:00 UTC: from staking transactions accepted before it

fields.name: node_age_weeks
fields.derivation: cutoff minus first_start_known, gaps included: span (G18); the named alternative is days_staked_weeks

fields.name: days_staked_weeks
fields.derivation: validating time before the cutoff, overlapping periods counted once, gaps excluded (G19)

fields.name: completed_periods
fields.derivation: validator periods ended by the cutoff: past_stint_count as decided in SD9

fields.name: started_periods
fields.derivation: validator periods started before the cutoff, the current one included: the named alternative

fields.name: reward_address_asof
fields.derivation: reward address of the node's latest validator transaction known at the week's cutoff, Monday 00:00 UTC: from staking transactions accepted before it; an operator proxy, not an identity

fields.name: delegated_avax_at_week_start
fields.derivation: stake of delegations to the active period, accepted before the cutoff, spanning it

fields.name: max_delegated_avax_14d
fields.derivation: largest delegated stake on the active period at the cutoff or at any scheduled start of a known delegation in the next 14 days

fields.name: max_weight_avax
fields.derivation: min(5 x self_stake_avax, 3,000,000): the validator's weight limit, self-stake included (AvalancheGo MaxValidatorWeightFactor and MaxValidatorStake)

fields.name: capacity_left_avax
fields.derivation: max_weight_avax minus self-stake minus delegated_avax_at_week_start

fields.name: capacity_left_avax_14d
fields.derivation: max_weight_avax minus self-stake minus max_delegated_avax_14d

fields.name: delegations_all
fields.derivation: delegations to the node accepted during the week

fields.name: delegated_avax_all
fields.derivation: their stake

fields.name: delegations_excl_concentrated
fields.derivation: the same without the concentrated address avax1tnuesf6cqwnjw7fxjyk7lhch0vhf0v95wj5jvy (decision SD8)

fields.name: delegated_avax_excl_concentrated
fields.derivation: their stake

fields.name: supply_counter_avax
fields.derivation: the P-Chain supply counter at its last reading before the cutoff: the supply the reward formula uses (decision RD8); null in the first week, before any reading

fields.name: supply_read_at
fields.derivation: acceptance time of the staking transaction that reading comes from

fields.name: gross_rate_14d
fields.derivation: the protocol kernel's annualized reward rate (annualized_reward_rate) of a 25 AVAX delegation starting at the cutoff, against supply_counter_avax (decision SD9), for fourteen days, the shortest delegation; active rows only

fields.name: net_rate_14d
fields.derivation: gross_rate_14d times one minus delegation_fee_rate

fields.name: log_net_apy_14d
fields.derivation: ln(net_rate_14d) when positive; null at a 100% fee, which stays an offer

fields.name: gross_rate_remaining
fields.derivation: the protocol kernel's annualized reward rate (annualized_reward_rate) of a 25 AVAX delegation starting at the cutoff, against supply_counter_avax (decision SD9), for the time left in the node's period, the longest delegation it can take; null under fourteen days

fields.name: net_rate_remaining
fields.derivation: gross_rate_remaining times one minus delegation_fee_rate

fields.name: log_net_apy_remaining
fields.derivation: ln(net_rate_remaining) when positive

datasets.name: Observed delegations of the validator-week window

fields.name: transaction_hash

fields.name: node_id

fields.derivation: the delegator is avax1tnuesf6cqwnjw7fxjyk7lhch0vhf0v95wj5jvy (decision SD8)

fields.name: accepted_at
fields.derivation: acceptance time of the transaction

fields.name: week_start_utc

fields.name: end_time

fields.name: stake_avax

fields.name: validator_offered_at_week_start
fields.derivation: that row's offered_at_week_start

fields.name: not_in_week_start_risk_set

datasets.name: AVAX monetary daily ledger
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
Value Accrual as Equilibrium: How We Think About AVAX Tokenomics
From Gross Chain Product to Gross Chain Income: Where the Value Goes
datasets.description: One row per UTC date with staking rewards paid out, AVAX burned on the P-, X-, and C-Chains, the realized total supply replayed from genesis, and the validator and delegated stake active at the end of the day, every amount an integer number of wei, with a coverage state per component. Supply is written only through the last day before the first incomplete one; nothing is imputed.

fields.name: date_utc
fields.derivation: one row per calendar day from the 2020-09-10 genesis to the last complete day of the P and X burn run

fields.name: issued_rewards_wei
fields.derivation: staking rewards paid out that day: realized reward UTXOs of the reward transactions accepted on the day, from snowflake.primary-staking-rewards, times 10^9; a validator's share of its delegators' fees is inside the validator's reward and counted once

fields.name: burned_p_wei
fields.derivation: burned_p_transactions_wei plus burned_p_l1_validator_fees_wei: the P-Chain burn as the Data API's totalPBurned defines it

fields.name: burned_p_transactions_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX destroyed by P-Chain transactions accepted that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, plus the burns of that day's unresolved transactions settled by p-chain-rpc.transactions, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_p_l1_validator_fees_wei
fields.derivation: L1 validator fees burned from validator balances that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_x_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX destroyed by X-Chain transactions accepted that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_c_evm_wei
fields.derivation: C-Chain EVM fees of the day's blocks: the share's complete blocks from snowflake.c-chain-evm-burn-daily plus burned_c_evm_gap_wei

fields.name: burned_c_evm_gap_wei
fields.derivation: fees of the day's gap blocks read from the Data API block record (data-api.c-chain-block-fees), a public node's receipts (c-chain-rpc.block-receipt-fees), or the archived node receipts (c-chain-rpc.receipt-gap-repairs), dated by the block's own timestamp; where two sources hold a block they must agree to the wei

fields.name: burned_c_atomic_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX unlocked minus created by the day's C-Chain imports and exports, from data-api.c-chain-atomic-burn, with each import the API leaves unsettled taken from c-chain-rpc.atomic-transactions, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_wei
fields.derivation: burned_p_wei + burned_x_wei + burned_c_evm_wei + burned_c_atomic_wei

fields.name: total_supply_open_wei
fields.derivation: the previous day's total_supply_close_wei; 360,000,000 AVAX on the genesis day

fields.name: total_supply_close_wei
fields.derivation: total_supply_open_wei + issued_rewards_wei - burned_wei, written only while every day from genesis through this one is complete, null after the first incomplete day

fields.name: active_validator_stake_wei
fields.derivation: self-stake of validator periods with start_time <= 23:59:59 UTC of the day < end_time, from derived.staking-periods, times 10^9

fields.name: active_delegated_stake_wei
fields.derivation: stake of delegator periods active at the same instant, times 10^9

fields.name: active_validators
fields.derivation: validator periods active at the instant

fields.name: active_delegations

datasets.name: Cycles of ACP-236 auto-renewed validators, from a P-Chain walk
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per cycle of each ACP-236 auto-renewed validator that a p-chain-rpc.blocks walk sees start, from Helicon on. The replay that rebuilds the supply counter models each cycle end as AvalancheGo v1.15.0 does: an abort forfeits the cycle's reward and ends the validator, a commit with a next period restakes the auto-compound share of the reward and of the delegation fees and starts the next cycle at the end of this one, and a commit without one ends the validator. The running cycle has null outcome columns. The share has no counterpart, since a cycle end is a RewardAutoRenewedValidatorTx.

fields.name: validator_transaction_hash
fields.derivation: the AddAutoRenewedValidatorTx that started the validator; every cycle keeps it

fields.name: node_id
fields.derivation: the transaction's nodeID

fields.name: cycle
fields.derivation: 1 for the cycle the transaction started, then one more per renewal

fields.name: start_time
fields.derivation: the accepting block's time for cycle 1, the previous cycle's end after

fields.name: end_time
fields.derivation: start plus the period in effect; equals the timestamp of the reward transaction that ends it

fields.name: weight_navax
fields.derivation: the stake of the cycle: the staked outputs for cycle 1, then the previous weight plus both restaked amounts

fields.name: potential_reward_navax
fields.derivation: protocol.start_stake or auto_renew_next_cycle on the replayed supply counter at the cycle's start

fields.name: auto_compound_shares
fields.derivation: the share of rewards restaked, from the transaction or a later SetAutoRenewedValidatorConfigTx

fields.name: next_period_seconds
fields.derivation: the period in effect at the cycle's end, 0 for a graceful exit; null while running

fields.name: reward_transaction_hash
fields.derivation: the RewardAutoRenewedValidatorTx that ended the cycle; null while running

fields.name: rewarded
fields.derivation: true after a commit, false after an abort; null while running

fields.name: delegatee_reward_navax
fields.derivation: the fee shares of delegations to the validator committed during the cycle

fields.name: restaked_validation_navax
fields.derivation: the part of the cycle's reward added to the next cycle's weight

fields.name: restaked_delegatee_navax
fields.derivation: the part of the delegation fees added to the next cycle's weight

fields.name: withdrawn_validation_navax
fields.derivation: the part of the cycle's reward paid out

fields.name: withdrawn_delegatee_navax
